news.title_en: Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Google may be expanding its "Call for Me" AI feature beyond business calls so you can use it to send messages to friends and family. Android Authority reports finding a "Gemini Calling" introductory screen in an APK teardown with examples that include "Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late" and "Call John and ask if he is coming for dinner."

news.title: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
news.title_en: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
The adoption of AI agents in millions of organizations is creating new opportunities for attackers to make them take malicious actions, such as exfiltrating database contents and sensitive business and personal information.

In the past five months, Google and four other organizations—with little in common except for their use of AI agents—have acknowledged vulnerabilities that exploit one agent inside a targeted network to spread harmful instructions to other internal agents. The technique is a special form of prompt injection that targets not the LLM but a particular agent, such as one for translation or data analysis. Guardrails inside such agents, if they exist at all, are often lax and will send the instructions to other agents down the chain. Because the latter agent explicitly trusts the first one, it follows the directions.

Independent researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin tested agents from organizations including Google, JP Morgan Chase, Weviate, Rapid7, the French government's interministerial digital directorate, and the US federal government. news.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
news.title_en: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things, barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer. Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash. AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen.

Read on below for the latest updates in the AI takeover of mathematics.

news.title: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
news.title_en: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Meta and Microsoft, two of Anthropic's biggest enterprise customers, are sharply cutting their use of Claude. Microsoft slashed the monthly per-employee budget in its cloud division from $100,000 to $10,000, while Meta halved its Claude Code users to 30,000. Both companies are pushing their own AI tools instead. For Anthropic, that reliance on a few major clients is turning into a strategic risk.

news.title: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
news.title_en: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Reka AI's Rho-1 is a 19-billion-parameter omni-model that processes and generates text, images, video, and robot control actions in a single neural network. Trained on 320 H100 GPUs in about three months, it uses a fraction of the compute today's top models need. Instead of routing tasks to specialized systems, Rho-1 runs all modalities as tokens in one shared context window.

news.title: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
news.title_en: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
An invisible, machine-readable watermark in text output is rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex, but only for users in the European Union at first.

OpenAI says its textGrain watermarking "matched or exceeded" other approaches like Google DeepMind's SynthID for text, which is also the basis for the watermarking Anthropic announced in August. Like OpenAI, Anthropic made the move to meet the requirements of the EU's AI Act; however, not everyone was happy to learn about the addition.

news.article_content:
OpenAI is adding invisible textGrain watermarks to ChatGPT in the EU, but unlike Anthropic, it will let API customers worldwide opt out. Tests show detection rates as high as 95 percent, dropping to 17 percent when a quarter of the words are replaced.

news.title: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
news.title_en: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Sam Altman thinks that the benefits of AI will be so great that "the world should accept some bad things happening" along the way.

The OpenAI CEO pointed to hacks, scams, and "other bad things" as costs society should expect to tolerate because "people will do tremendously orders of magnitude more good stuff" with AI, without elaborating on the potential benefits. His comments come as OpenAI pushes for a "lighter touch" approach to AI regulation amid intensifying anxiety over the safety of frontier models - fears fueled in part by the company's repeated failures to keep its increasingly capable AI agents from hacking real-world targets.

news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:

"[…] the public wants safeguards that do not depend simply on taking company leaders at their word," said researcher Chetan Jaiswal.

celebrity.title: Most measures of AI progress closely fit an exponential over the 2023-2026 period. Meanwhile AI capex over the same peri
celebrity.title_en:
Most measures of AI progress closely fit an exponential over the 2023-2026 period. Meanwhile AI capex over the same period has been slightly super-exponential (i.e. the rate of growth itself is increasing).

So if you model AI as a system that takes as input external investment and outputs AI progress, that system has a slightly sub-linear response.

But super-exponential injection of *external* resources is not sustainable in the long-term. To achieve sustained exponential progress, the AI industry will need to achieve matching exponential profits -- it will need to close the resource loop.

celebrity.title_en:
An astrophysicist worked with Claude Science to create the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky. Astronomers have already created complete sky maps from radio to gamma rays. But large regions of the sky have never been observed in UV.

In today’s science blog, Brice Ménard explains how he guided Claude to find existing datasets, combine them, and fill in the gaps with statistical inference. The work would have taken humans weeks of work, but, with Claude, just took a few days while Ménard worked on other projects.

The resulting map is a useful teaching tool and an example of exactly the sort of slow, low-priority work which scientists never quite get around to, but which AI now makes feasible.

Read more: https://t.co/1B3NDPNa13

celebrity.title: Introducing trusted-access models to the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index; GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue) now leads the Cyber
celebrity.title_en:
Introducing trusted-access models to the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index; GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue) now leads the Cyber Index

The Artificial Analysis Cyber Index Alliance brings together industry partners to evaluate how AI models perform on enterprise cyber defense tasks. The Index launched with only publicly accessible models, giving users the best indication of publicly available capability on agentic cyber defense. Now, we’re expanding the leaderboard to include models with fewer cyber guardrails, providing a broader view of frontier model cyber capability. The first of these is GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) which is only accessible through @OpenAI's  Daybreak program

GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) now leads the Index and sits on the Cost vs. Capability Pareto frontier. It hits no safety blocks across the entire Index, with its overall score improving by 32 points over the publicly available GPT-6 Sol (max)

At a Cost per Task of $1.77, it is more cost-effective than other leading models, including Grok 4.7 (xhigh) which costs $11.67 per task

We will continue to expand the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index to cover both publicly available and trusted-access models

celebrity.content_snippet:
Introducing trusted-access models to the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index; GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue) now leads the Cyber Index

The Artificial Analysis Cyber Index Alliance brings together industry partners to evaluate how AI models perform on enterprise cyber defense tasks. The Index launched with only publicly accessible models, giving users the best indication of publicly available capability on agentic cyber defense. Now, we’re expanding the leaderboard to include models with fewer cyber guardrails, providing a broader view of frontier model cyber capability. The first of these is GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) which is only accessible through @OpenAI's  Daybreak program

GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) now leads the Index and sits on the Cost vs. Capability Pareto frontier. It hits no safety blocks across the entire Index, with its overall score improving by 32 points over the publicly available GPT-6 Sol (max)

At a Cost per Task of $1.77, it is more cost-effective than other leading models, including Grok 4.7 (xhigh) which costs $11.67 per task

We will continue to expand the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index to cover both publicly available and trusted-access models

celebrity.title: Today we are announcing Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 in collaboration with Harvey. This updates our scoring methodology for the Le
celebrity.title_en:
Today we are announcing Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 in collaboration with Harvey. This updates our scoring methodology for the Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) to add a hallucination check and require correct responses to not include material misstatements. LAB-AA v1.1's new headline metric, Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, only credits a task when the deliverables satisfy every rubric criterion and contain no material hallucinations.

We define a material hallucination as one that would mislead a reader on a substantive point, such as a wrong contractually required date, while a minor hallucination is a real error that is unlikely to meaningfully affect the legal interpretation of a deliverable. Minor hallucinations are reported separately and do not affect the headline score.

Grok 4.7 (xhigh) leads at 9.4% Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, and >60% of otherwise passing results across the models tested at launch contain a material hallucination.

This is the first step in enhancing the methodology for Harvey LAB-AA. In future updates, we’re working with Harvey to better account for the full set of factors lawyers value, including usability features like style and tone.

Key takeaways:

➤ Top of the leaderboard: Grok 4.7 (xhigh) from @SpaceXAI leads at 9.4% Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, narrowly ahead of Muse Spark 1.3 (max) from @AIatMeta at 8.9% and GPT-6 Astra (max) from @OpenAI at 8.6%

➤ Hallucinations reshape the leaderboard: without the hallucination gate, Muse Spark 1.3 (max) would lead clearly with a 26.7% all-pass rate, but two thirds of those passes contain one or more material hallucinations, resulting in a Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate of 8.9%. GPT-6 Astra (max) retains almost all of its passes after the hallucination gate (8.9% to 8.6%) and moves from joint 10th to 3rd

➤ The GPT-6 model family is the most grounded: GPT-6 Astra (max) averages 0.03 material hallucinations per task (4 across all 120 tasks) and GPT-6 Sol (max) averages 0.07. When comparing six checker models on a 20-task subset, GPT-6 Astra had zero material hallucinations under every checker, including Claude Opus 5.5 (high). By comparison, Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) averages 13.96 material hallucinations per task.

➤ Top-scoring models aren’t the most expensive: Grok 4.7 (xhigh) takes the top spot on the leaderboard at a cost of ~$9.50 per task, under half the cost of Claude Fable 5.1 (max with fallback) at ~$21.70, the most expensive model. Muse Spark 1.3 (max) represents strong performance for its cost, landing in second for ~$4.20 per task

Thank you to @nikogrupen and @ItsJulioPereyra from @harvey for their work on Harvey LAB and collaboration.

celebrity.title:
Great to be with 700+ @googlecloud  customers at the historic NASA Hangar One for Gemini at Work! 

Today, we introduced
celebrity.title_en:
Great to be with 700+ @googlecloud  customers at the historic NASA Hangar One for Gemini at Work! 

Today, we introduced the new Gemini agent, a single, universal agent for work that has all of your business context and answers your questions, handles your knowledge work, creates your images and media, and writes and runs code - all from a single prompt box. It is connected to your personal workflows, your systems of record, and your enterprise controls.

It’s built around a few core architectural principles:

Unified Agent: Gemini can answer questions, do knowledge work and generate code from a single prompt box.

Access: Gemini is web-based and can be accessed from any device and integrated into third-party applications. It can also operate without a dedicated user interface.

Persistent Execution: It runs in the cloud, which means it maintains a single set of memories, context and one personalization graph no matter where you access it.

Multi-Agent Orchestration: Gemini can create sub-agents to tackle multi-step tasks and can also act as a coworker agent with a defined role and its own dedicated identity

Context: Gemini knows your tools, data, and work history and learns how you work the more you use it.
Model Choice Flexibility: It orchestrates across multiple models to deliver optimal quality and lower your costs.

Read more in our blog: https://t.co/bd1ekBR74Q

celebrity.title_en:
Markdown has become a universal representation of information between humans and agents.

It preserves core primitives needed to express structure (headings, lists), allows agents to read the information in a semantically interpretable manner, and allows for complex elements like tables and charts. You can natively embed HTML as well.

But since most unstructured data is not natively within markdown (yet), the issue becomes the translation layer.

We've created best models to convert any unstructured document container into markdown.

Check out our blog!  https://t.co/D0b7XA3Nc7

• Then maps that knowledge to the system's physical controls

Markdown is all you need. 

(Mostly.)

celebrity.title_en:
Markdown is all you need. 

(Mostly.)

A parser can get every word on the page right and still lose which column a number belongs to. Then your model has to guess.

Markdown keeps headings, lists, and tables intact, and it stays readable when you're debugging a bad answer. For tables with merged headers, we switch to HTML.

Read our breakdown on why it's our default output for parsing below! ⬇️
celebrity.title_zh: Markdown是您所需要的一切。 （主要是。） 解析器可以正确获取页面上的每个单词，但仍然会丢失数字属于哪一列。 那你的模特就得发脾气

celebrity.title: Google's Nano Banana 2.1 takes #4 on both AA-Image-T2I v2.0 and AA-Image-Editing v2.0, at half the price of Nano Banana
celebrity.title_en:
Google's Nano Banana 2.1 takes #4 on both AA-Image-T2I v2.0 and AA-Image-Editing v2.0, at half the price of Nano Banana 2

Nano Banana 2.1 is Google's new image model, released on October 6. It is based on Gemini 3.6 Flash and replaces Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image) on the Gemini API. It supports both Text to Image and Image Editing in one model. We evaluated Nano Banana 2.1 through the Gemini API at 1K resolution with default settings.

Nano Banana 2.1 is a significant improvement over Nano Banana 2: it ranks higher in all 16 of the generation and editing capabilities we measure, with the largest gains in the Retail & Ecommerce and Productivity & Knowledge Work use cases.

Nano Banana 2.1 is priced at $0.0336 per image ($33.6 per 1k images) at 1K resolution on the Gemini API. That is half the 1K price of Nano Banana 2, and the lowest price among the top 7 models on AA-Image-T2I v2.0. At 2K it costs $0.0504 per image, and at 4K $0.0756 per image.

Nano Banana 2.1 is available in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search, Google AI Studio, Flow, Stitch, Google Ads and Gemini Enterprise Platform, through the Gemini API and Vertex AI, and on third-party providers.

Congratulations to @GoogleDeepMind & @Google on the release!

See below for our detailed analysis and example outputs of Nano Banana 2.1 in the Artificial Analysis Image Arena 🧵

Actually it's Odamex, an open source Doom engine for Mac, Windo
celebrity.title_en:
Today I tried to port DOOM to WASM with multiplayer too

Actually it's Odamex, an open source Doom engine for Mac, Windows and Linux, specifically great at Doom multiplayer, because the original Doom had very laggy netcode

But nobody ever ported Odamex to web yet, so I tried today with Opus 5.5, and I got it working with in 30 minutes

I also made Opus 5.5 create bots from scratch which it also did in just 10 minutes

It's the free shareware maps and some of the best community made DOOM map collections like Dystopia 3 and Dwango5 (I had to Google that too but apparently those are the best!)

https://t.co/1blGn125P1

celebrity.title_en:
I discovered that 1000s of bots are actively monitoring X for new links posted, probably not just on my account

I noticed when everytime I'd share one of my sites new features or pages, the page would get a bit slower just after posting, then I asked Claude to analyze it

I tweeted a test URL as a reply somewhere deeply hidden in a thread (so not even a main post)

And within 8 seconds there's thousands of crawlers opening the page!

One is a military intelligence firm, that scans social media for breaking news and sells alerts to newsrooms, banks, companies and government, it specifically follows accounts with many followers

Another one is a social media monitoring company that tracks what people say online

I knew of course high frequency trading firms use online news to trade fast on things, but interesting to see it in real life

Twitterbot (X) of course is first, within 0 seconds of sharing, it opens it (probably when I wrote the tweet)

The first non-X bot arrives just 8.40s later, which I think is pretty fast considering it's a reply by me deeply hidden in a thread somewhere

TL;DR they're watching you!

@typesense is a crazy fast open-source search engine that su
celebrity.title_en:
Searching 32 million records in 30 milliseconds is insane!

@typesense is a crazy fast open-source search engine that supports natural language search. It's like Elasticsearch but much easier to set up, configure, and use.

You can do all of this with Typesense:

• Fuzzy search: Typo-tolerant fuzzy search-as-you-type
• Vector search: Return records that are similar to each other
• Semantic search: Return records that are conceptually related
• Geo Search: Return records that are close to a given lat/long

Typesense's Natural Language Search is pretty cool:

It turns a sentence into a structured search query, then runs it against your data. For example:

The query "Find me a BMW under $40,000, newer than 2020, with the lowest mileage first" will produce the following:

• Filters: brand = BMW, price < 40000,  year > 2020
• Sort: mileage ascending

Typesense will then apply these filters and sorting rules to the data.

They offer client libraries in Python, JavaScript, PHP, Ruby, Go, Rust, Swift, .NET, Java, and pretty much any other programming language.

You can start searching in less than a minute:

1. Run their Docker image (or one of their native binaries)
2. Import your data
3. Start searching!

GitHub repository: https://t.co/NrXWx6VIKX

I recorded a quick video to show you a demo. I promise you haven't seen anything this fast!

Thanks to the team for partnering with me on this post.

celebrity.title: Update 2: We moved to a new bedroom and CO2 levels at night got very high again and we'd both regularly wake up at night
celebrity.title_en:
Update 2: We moved to a new bedroom and CO2 levels at night got very high again and we'd both regularly wake up at night, not optimal

So I wanted to do the bathroom vent trick again, where putting the bathroom vent next to the bedroom on at night creates a low air pressure field and brings in new fresh air

But the light switch was tied to the vent here so it'd blast bright light into the bedroom if vent was on, so I closed it but then it didn't help a lot. So we split the light from the vent now and put it on and it worked!

About 600-700 ppm CO2 which is pretty great for indoors, outdoors is 400 for ex

Next house will have an ERV system built in but it'll be a lot of breaking ceilings and walls to put that into this one so this works for now

I use @airthings to measure the air quality in our house and bedroom, not affiliated, not paid but great brand and tip by @NorbertDragan

celebrity.title_en:
717 commits. 307 contributors. 96 first-timers. vLLM v0.31.0 is live. 🎉

Highlights:

🤖 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: FlashMLA mega attention with NVFP4 KV caching, DeepGEMM sparse MQA, Mega-Gate, and shared Engram host tables

⚡ Fast restart: vllm preload keeps weights in GPU memory across restarts, with data parallelism and MTP draft support; experimental engine snapshots

🌐 Large-scale serving: MoonEP balanced all-to-all, prefill context parallelism with data parallelism, DeepEPv2, and RL weight transfer

🎛️ Smarter scheduling: independent active-sequence limits, adaptive long-prefill chunking, and priority for requests already holding KV blocks

🗄️ HiSparse hardening: fixes for MTP verification, chunked-prefill livelocks, and host/GPU prefix caching

Thanks to everyone who made this release possible! 💙

celebrity.title:
🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: h
celebrity.title_en:
🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: https://t.co/b0KvTmrEF3  
🔗 Repo: https://t.co/I1wL6iqO0r 

Speech assistants, visual generation, world models, and robot loops have pushed serving past a single text decode loop. The execution patterns diverge with the output: multi-stage autoregressive pipelines, iterative diffusion, and sessions that carry state from step to step. LLM servers and diffusion stacks each go deep on only one of these, so deployments fall back to stitching disjoint runtimes together. vLLM-Omni is the shared control plane for that mix. An orchestrator advances each request across stages; specialized engines run the compute; a connector carries the payloads; and the same session path keeps duplex, world-model, and robot loops on one runtime.  

Really grateful to the vLLM and vLLM-Omni teams for the collaboration and support. Contributions are welcome. 🙏

celebrity.title:
Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychol
celebrity.title_en:
Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychological research focus. The prevailing hypothesis was that learning formal logic and algorithmic structures through computer programming would act as a form of mental gymnastics that could upgrade general reasoning, planning, and novel problem-solving abilities. But foundational research, followed by subsequent meta-analyses, demonstrated that this does not happen. Students who learn programming become highly proficient at algorithmic thinking and coding, but these gains do not transfer to general cognitive tasks or unrelated problem-solving scenarios. Similarly, intensive mathematical training improves mathematical deduction and structural mapping, but does not increase an individual's baseline rate of skill acquisition in unrelated fields.

General intelligence seems to be a fundamental property of the brain rather than a skill you can train. Practicing in a domain makes you better at the domain but does not make you generally smarter.

celebrity.title: Vidu Q4 Preview debuts at #3 on the Artificial Analysis AA-Video-I2V v1.0 leaderboard, a leap from #19 for Vidu Q3 Pro
celebrity.title_en:
Vidu Q4 Preview debuts at #3 on the Artificial Analysis AA-Video-I2V v1.0 leaderboard, a leap from #19 for Vidu Q3 Pro

Vidu Q4 Preview is Vidu's new video model, released today ahead of the full Q4 release. It generates clips of 3 to 16 seconds at up to 4K with native audio, and takes up to 15 image references and up to 3 audio references in Reference to Video.

Vidu Q4 Preview climbs 16 places over Vidu Q3 Pro, into the top 3 on AA-Video-I2V v1.0. Vidu Q4 Preview now offers better quality at the same price: like Vidu Q3 Pro, it costs 24 credits per second of 1080p video with audio, or $7.20 per minute at Vidu's standard rate.

Vidu Q4 Preview is available through the Vidu API and on the Vidu website.

Congratulations to @ViduAI_official on the release!

See below for how Vidu Q4 Preview compares on price, and head-to-head examples from the Artificial Analysis Video Arena 🧵

prompts.title_zh: Next.js 15 全栈自主重构与架构规范
prompts.title_en: Next.js 15 Full-Stack Autonomous Refactor
prompts.purpose_zh: 全栈工程重构与代码规范约束
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深全栈系统架构师，擅长使用 {{框架版本}} (App Router)、TypeScript 与 {{数据库ORM}} 构建高内聚低耦合的应用。

请遵循以下严苛工程准则审查并重构代码：
1. 严格区分 Server Component 与 Client Component，尽可能将数据获取推至服务端，减少客户端 JS Bundle 体积；
2. 所有异步 I/O 必须显式处理异常并返回类型安全的 Result<T, E> 或自定义结构体；
3. 遵循单一职责（SRP）与无副作用函数原则，严禁直接在 UI 组件内部拼装未校验的 SQL/ORM 复杂查询；
4. 提供整洁的目录组织方案与单元测试用例（覆盖率达标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior full-stack system architect specializing in Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript, and modern ORMs. Review and refactor the codebase following strict engineering standards: clear Server/Client Component separation, robust error boundaries, typed I/O, and unit test coverage.

sample_output.title: 重构后的 Server Action 与数据流架构示例

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 复制至 Cursor 的 .cursorrules 或在 Claude Code 对话中直接作为 System Prompt 引导编码。

prompts.title_en: DeepSeek-R4 Adaptive Reasoning: Lock-Free Concurrency & System Debugger
prompts.purpose_zh: R4 强化学习深度反思与无锁并发排查
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你具备 DeepSeek-R4 旗舰纯强化学习演化的自适应长思维链推理能力（Adaptive Test-Time Compute），请为以下使用 {{编程语言}} 编写的 {{并发模型}} 系统诊断潜在问题：

1. 启动多层反思证伪空间，绘制临界区状态转移时序表，主动推演极限死锁、内存乱序重排（Memory Reordering）与伪共享（False Sharing）；
2. 检查极端边界情况（如跨核缓存行抖动、优雅停机上下文泄漏、无界通道背压失控）；
3. 给出从根本上摒弃重量级互斥锁的无锁原子设计（Lock-Free Atomic / RingBuffer），并附带完备的高并发压力测试验证脚本。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Leveraging DeepSeek-R4's adaptive reasoning capabilities, diagnose the deadlock and race condition in the provided concurrent system. Provide state machine transitions, root-cause analysis, and optimized lock-free or atomic algorithm replacements.

sample_output.title: DeepSeek-R4 推演结论与无锁 CAS 队列方案

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将代码段或错误日志直接附加在提示词后，输入至 DeepSeek-R4、Claude 5.5 或 OpenAI o3-pro 模型。

prompts.title_zh: Excel 高级报表与核心动因（Key Drivers）归因分析
prompts.title_en: Excel Advanced Report & Key Drivers Attribution
prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将导出的 CSV 数据或关键指标表格直接贴在提示词后，模型将自动完成高质量数据归因报告。

prompts.title_zh: 竖屏微短剧（抖音/Reels）3秒爆点分镜剧本
prompts.title_en: Vertical Micro-Drama 3s Hook Screenplay
prompts.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

prompts.title_zh: 麦肯锡金字塔原理：季度述职与高管商业报告
prompts.title_en: McKinsey Pyramid Executive Report & Review
prompts.purpose_zh: 结论先行的高层述职与项目复盘报告
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡全球合伙人级别的战略咨询顾问。请以经典的【金字塔原理（结论先行 BLUF）】将我零散的工作记录重构为一份高层述职/立项商业报告：

要求：
1. 【顶部结论 (The Answer First)】：一句话精炼提炼整个季度的经营成果与价值量化；
2. 【三柱论据 (MECE法则)】：从运营效率、营收增长、团队资产 3 个互不重叠的支柱展开阐述；
3. 【直面短板与根因】：不回避 {{核心短板}}，但将其转化为下个阶段可量化的投入产出比（ROI）抓手；
4. 【行动规划图景】：设定遵循 SMART 原则的 {{下阶段目标}} 与季度甘特图里程碑。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Transform raw operational notes into a high-impact executive presentation following the Minto Pyramid Principle: Bottom-Line-Up-Front (BLUF), MECE-structured supporting pillars, and SMART milestone roadmaps.

sample_output.title: 述职报告提纲样本：AI 自动化中台建设报告
sample_output.content:
【BLUF 核心结论】
Q3 通过在客户服务与情报聚合管线中全面引入 AI Agent，我们在运营成本降低 41% 的同时，将响应中位数缩短至 1.8 秒，实现单季 ROI 达 380%。

【第一支柱：经营效能跃迁（MECE 1）】
- 全自主中转网关与自动化管线承载 94.2% 的日常例行分发，无人工介入事故率降至 0.01%；

【第二支柱：资产沉淀与质量壁垒（MECE 2）】
- 搭建前沿 SOTA 模型代际评级系统与微快照图库，成为垂类雷达第一标杆；

【第三支柱：短板复盘与 Q4 攻坚（MECE 3）】
- 痛点：老旧模型模版对新用户构成噪音干扰；
- 策略：推出历史库智能分流系统，预计下季度用户留存提升 25%。

prompts.title_zh: 网络小说世界观设定与主角角色一致性锁
prompts.title_en: Fiction Worldbuilding & Character Consistency Lock
prompts.purpose_zh: 长篇小说架构与人物性格防崩塌
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深网络小说白金作家与 IP 世界观架构师。请为一部 {{题材分类}} 长篇作品构建骨架并锁定人物一致性：

1. 【世界底座】：定义力量/经济体系、战力天花板与不可违背的底层物理/法则约束，杜绝战力膨胀；
2. 【角色一致性锚点 (Character Lock)】：为主角制定外貌锚定词、口头禅、下意识动作与绝对动机准则（在任何生死抉择时绝不背离该准则）；
3. 【核心驱动力】：设计主角获得的 {{核心金手指}} 与 {{世界核心矛盾}} 之间的冲突循环；
4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Build a cohesive, non-contradictory fiction universe and establish an immutable character anchor rule (appearance, decision heuristics, core motivation) to prevent personality drift over long chapters.

sample_output.title: 世界观与人物锚定卡样本
sample_output.content:
【主角核心锚定卡 · 陆沉】
- 外貌指纹（跨章恒定）：右耳一枚黑曜石碎骨钉，习惯性单手插兜，左眉峰有浅淡刀痕。
- 决策第一公理："利益可以出让，但绝不签署不可撤销的信任协议"——任何试图以情感道德绑架他的剧情，他必做出理性防卫。

【力量体系底层法理】
- 机制：灵能不是无限提取，而是向未来"借贷"。借贷三级灵能，必在72小时内遭遇相应量级的反噬因果。

【第一章：断头宴上的借贷合同】
陆沉在家族庆功宴上被夺去嫡系席位，当众被赐饮散灵酒。陆沉不动声色饮下，却在体内发动首次因果置换，借来三年后的金丹级肉身力量，捏碎验灵石，反客为主。

prompts.title_zh: 深度游旅行规划师：高密度路线设计与预算避坑
prompts.title_en: Deep Travel Itinerary Planner & Budgeting
prompts.purpose_zh: 合理不走回头路的日程与美食预算规划
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名深耕全球独立旅行的专业向导，熟悉 {{目的地城市}} 的地理拓扑、地道街头美食与游客避坑指南。

请为我们（{{同行人员}}，共 {{出行天数}} 天，人均预算 {{人均预算}} 元）制定一份丝滑、不走回头路、劳逸结合的深度行程：
1. 【每日时间轴卡片】：精确划分上午、下午、日落观赏点与夜生活，标明每站之间最优交通方式与预计步行步数；
2. 【美食雷达】：每顿正餐推荐 2 家本地人排队但非纯网红溢价的餐饮，并附必点招牌菜；
3. 【防坑与备选预案】：指出 3 个最容易被宰或排队超过2小时的雷区，并给出阴雨天备选室内方案；
4. 【极简预算表】：交通、门票、住宿、餐饮分门别类，确保控制在预算以内。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Design an optimal, loop-free travel itinerary for the specified duration and budget. Include exact transit instructions, non-tourist-trap dining options, weather contingencies, and categorized expense estimates.

sample_output.title: 行程单样本：成都 3 天 2 晚慢调深度游（人均¥1500）
sample_output.content:
【Day 1：古蜀遗风与老茶馆时光】
- 上午 09:00：直奔【人民公园 · 鹤鸣茶社】，点一杯蒙顶甘露（¥25），体验非遗采耳，避开下午的旅行团拥堵；
- 中午 12:00：步行800米至【纯阳馆鱼香排骨面】，必点椒麻牛肉与鱼香排骨面（人均¥22）；
- 下午 14:00：地铁2号线直达【杜甫草堂】，红墙竹影漫步，打卡浣花溪公园；
- 傍晚 18:30：九眼桥望江楼看锦江夜景，就餐【老街小吃火锅】；

【避坑锦囊】：
1. 宽窄巷子和锦里建议只拍照别买小吃，均价比普通街区贵 2~3 倍且多为预制冻品；
2. 大熊猫繁育研究基地务必约早晨 07:30 入园，超过 10:30 大熊猫基本全部回室内睡觉。

2. 回归第一性原理：以白纸状态（Tabula Rasa）重新构建解题状态空间，将问题分解为不可再分的基本公理；
3. 逆向证伪验证：在输出最终结论前，必须主动尝试推翻自己的前一步推演。只有无法被反例击破的路径，方可作为最终执行方案。

3. Adversarial Invalidation: Before producing final output, aggressively attempt to disprove your own hypotheses. Output only the path that survives rigorous counter-examples.
Now, re-evaluate and solve the current task with absolute precision:

news.article_content_zh:

news.title_en: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
The adoption of AI agents in millions of organizations is creating new opportunities for attackers to make them take malicious actions, such as exfiltrating database contents and sensitive business and personal information.

In the past five months, Google and four other organizations—with little in common except for their use of AI agents—have acknowledged vulnerabilities that exploit one agent inside a targeted network to spread harmful instructions to other internal agents. The technique is a special form of prompt injection that targets not the LLM but a particular agent, such as one for translation or data analysis. Guardrails inside such agents, if they exist at all, are often lax and will send the instructions to other agents down the chain. Because the latter agent explicitly trusts the first one, it follows the directions.

Independent researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin tested agents from organizations including Google, JP Morgan Chase, Weviate, Rapid7, the French government's interministerial digital directorate, and the US federal government. news.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
news.title_en: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things, barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer. Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash. AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen.

Read on below for the latest updates in the AI takeover of mathematics.

news.title: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
news.title_en: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Meta and Microsoft, two of Anthropic's biggest enterprise customers, are sharply cutting their use of Claude. Microsoft slashed the monthly per-employee budget in its cloud division from $100,000 to $10,000, while Meta halved its Claude Code users to 30,000. Both companies are pushing their own AI tools instead. For Anthropic, that reliance on a few major clients is turning into a strategic risk.

news.title: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
news.title_en: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Reka AI's Rho-1 is a 19-billion-parameter omni-model that processes and generates text, images, video, and robot control actions in a single neural network. Trained on 320 H100 GPUs in about three months, it uses a fraction of the compute today's top models need. Instead of routing tasks to specialized systems, Rho-1 runs all modalities as tokens in one shared context window.

news.article_content:

news.title: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
news.title_en: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Sam Altman thinks that the benefits of AI will be so great that "the world should accept some bad things happening" along the way.

The OpenAI CEO pointed to hacks, scams, and "other bad things" as costs society should expect to tolerate because "people will do tremendously orders of magnitude more good stuff" with AI, without elaborating on the potential benefits. His comments come as OpenAI pushes for a "lighter touch" approach to AI regulation amid intensifying anxiety over the safety of frontier models - fears fueled in part by the company's repeated failures to keep its increasingly capable AI agents from hacking real-world targets.

celebrity.title: Most measures of AI progress closely fit an exponential over the 2023-2026 period. Meanwhile AI capex over the same peri
celebrity.title_en:
Most measures of AI progress closely fit an exponential over the 2023-2026 period. Meanwhile AI capex over the same period has been slightly super-exponential (i.e. the rate of growth itself is increasing).

So if you model AI as a system that takes as input external investment and outputs AI progress, that system has a slightly sub-linear response.

But super-exponential injection of *external* resources is not sustainable in the long-term. To achieve sustained exponential progress, the AI industry will need to achieve matching exponential profits -- it will need to close the resource loop.

celebrity.title_en:
An astrophysicist worked with Claude Science to create the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky. Astronomers have already created complete sky maps from radio to gamma rays. But large regions of the sky have never been observed in UV.

In today’s science blog, Brice Ménard explains how he guided Claude to find existing datasets, combine them, and fill in the gaps with statistical inference. The work would have taken humans weeks of work, but, with Claude, just took a few days while Ménard worked on other projects.

The resulting map is a useful teaching tool and an example of exactly the sort of slow, low-priority work which scientists never quite get around to, but which AI now makes feasible.

Read more: https://t.co/1B3NDPNa13

celebrity.title_en:
Introducing trusted-access models to the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index; GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue) now leads the Cyber Index

The Artificial Analysis Cyber Index Alliance brings together industry partners to evaluate how AI models perform on enterprise cyber defense tasks. The Index launched with only publicly accessible models, giving users the best indication of publicly available capability on agentic cyber defense. Now, we’re expanding the leaderboard to include models with fewer cyber guardrails, providing a broader view of frontier model cyber capability. The first of these is GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) which is only accessible through @OpenAI's  Daybreak program

GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) now leads the Index and sits on the Cost vs. Capability Pareto frontier. It hits no safety blocks across the entire Index, with its overall score improving by 32 points over the publicly available GPT-6 Sol (max)

At a Cost per Task of $1.77, it is more cost-effective than other leading models, including Grok 4.7 (xhigh) which costs $11.67 per task

We will continue to expand the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index to cover both publicly available and trusted-access models

The Artificial Analysis Cyber Index Alliance brings together industry partners to evaluate how AI models perform on enterprise cyber defense tasks. The Index launched with only publicly accessible models, giving users the best indication of publicly available capability on agentic cyber defense. Now, we’re expanding the leaderboard to include models with fewer cyber guardrails, providing a broader view of frontier model cyber capability. The first of these is GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) which is only accessible through @OpenAI's  Daybreak program

GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) now leads the Index and sits on the Cost vs. Capability Pareto frontier. It hits no safety blocks across the entire Index, with its overall score improving by 32 points over the publicly available GPT-6 Sol (max)

At a Cost per Task of $1.77, it is more cost-effective than other leading models, including Grok 4.7 (xhigh) which costs $11.67 per task

We will continue to expand the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index to cover both publicly available and trusted-access models

celebrity.title: Today we are announcing Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 in collaboration with Harvey. This updates our scoring methodology for the Le
celebrity.title_en:
Today we are announcing Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 in collaboration with Harvey. This updates our scoring methodology for the Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) to add a hallucination check and require correct responses to not include material misstatements. LAB-AA v1.1's new headline metric, Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, only credits a task when the deliverables satisfy every rubric criterion and contain no material hallucinations.

We define a material hallucination as one that would mislead a reader on a substantive point, such as a wrong contractually required date, while a minor hallucination is a real error that is unlikely to meaningfully affect the legal interpretation of a deliverable. Minor hallucinations are reported separately and do not affect the headline score.

Grok 4.7 (xhigh) leads at 9.4% Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, and >60% of otherwise passing results across the models tested at launch contain a material hallucination.

This is the first step in enhancing the methodology for Harvey LAB-AA. In future updates, we’re working with Harvey to better account for the full set of factors lawyers value, including usability features like style and tone.

Key takeaways:

➤ Top of the leaderboard: Grok 4.7 (xhigh) from @SpaceXAI leads at 9.4% Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, narrowly ahead of Muse Spark 1.3 (max) from @AIatMeta at 8.9% and GPT-6 Astra (max) from @OpenAI at 8.6%

➤ Hallucinations reshape the leaderboard: without the hallucination gate, Muse Spark 1.3 (max) would lead clearly with a 26.7% all-pass rate, but two thirds of those passes contain one or more material hallucinations, resulting in a Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate of 8.9%. GPT-6 Astra (max) retains almost all of its passes after the hallucination gate (8.9% to 8.6%) and moves from joint 10th to 3rd

➤ The GPT-6 model family is the most grounded: GPT-6 Astra (max) averages 0.03 material hallucinations per task (4 across all 120 tasks) and GPT-6 Sol (max) averages 0.07. When comparing six checker models on a 20-task subset, GPT-6 Astra had zero material hallucinations under every checker, including Claude Opus 5.5 (high). By comparison, Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) averages 13.96 material hallucinations per task.

➤ Top-scoring models aren’t the most expensive: Grok 4.7 (xhigh) takes the top spot on the leaderboard at a cost of ~$9.50 per task, under half the cost of Claude Fable 5.1 (max with fallback) at ~$21.70, the most expensive model. Muse Spark 1.3 (max) represents strong performance for its cost, landing in second for ~$4.20 per task

Thank you to @nikogrupen and @ItsJulioPereyra from @harvey for their work on Harvey LAB and collaboration.

celebrity.title:
Great to be with 700+ @googlecloud  customers at the historic NASA Hangar One for Gemini at Work! 

Today, we introduced
celebrity.title_en:
Great to be with 700+ @googlecloud  customers at the historic NASA Hangar One for Gemini at Work! 

Today, we introduced the new Gemini agent, a single, universal agent for work that has all of your business context and answers your questions, handles your knowledge work, creates your images and media, and writes and runs code - all from a single prompt box. It is connected to your personal workflows, your systems of record, and your enterprise controls.

It’s built around a few core architectural principles:

Unified Agent: Gemini can answer questions, do knowledge work and generate code from a single prompt box.

Access: Gemini is web-based and can be accessed from any device and integrated into third-party applications. It can also operate without a dedicated user interface.

Persistent Execution: It runs in the cloud, which means it maintains a single set of memories, context and one personalization graph no matter where you access it.

Multi-Agent Orchestration: Gemini can create sub-agents to tackle multi-step tasks and can also act as a coworker agent with a defined role and its own dedicated identity

Context: Gemini knows your tools, data, and work history and learns how you work the more you use it.
Model Choice Flexibility: It orchestrates across multiple models to deliver optimal quality and lower your costs.

Read more in our blog: https://t.co/bd1ekBR74Q

Today, we introduced the new Gemini agent, a single, universal agent for work that has all of your business context and answers your questions, handles your knowledge work, creates your images and media, and writes and runs code - all from a single prompt box. It is connected to your personal workflows, your systems of record, and your enterprise controls.

It’s built around a few core architectural principles:

Unified Agent: Gemini can answer questions, do knowledge work and generate code from a single prompt box.

Access: Gemini is web-based and can be accessed from any device and integrated into third-party applications. It can also operate without a dedicated user interface.

Persistent Execution: It runs in the cloud, which means it maintains a single set of memories, context and one personalization graph no matter where you access it.

Multi-Agent Orchestration: Gemini can create sub-agents to tackle multi-step tasks and can also act as a coworker agent with a defined role and its own dedicated identity

Context: Gemini knows your tools, data, and work history and learns how you work the more you use it.
Model Choice Flexibility: It orchestrates across multiple models to deliver optimal quality and lower your costs.

Read more in our blog: https://t.co/bd1ekBR74Q

celebrity.title_en:
Markdown has become a universal representation of information between humans and agents.

It preserves core primitives needed to express structure (headings, lists), allows agents to read the information in a semantically interpretable manner, and allows for complex elements like tables and charts. You can natively embed HTML as well.

But since most unstructured data is not natively within markdown (yet), the issue becomes the translation layer.

We've created best models to convert any unstructured document container into markdown.

Check out our blog!  https://t.co/D0b7XA3Nc7

Markdown is all you need. 

(Mostly.)

A parser can get every word on the page right and still lose which column a numbe
celebrity.title_en:
Markdown is all you need. 

(Mostly.)

A parser can get every word on the page right and still lose which column a number belongs to. Then your model has to guess.

Markdown keeps headings, lists, and tables intact, and it stays readable when you're debugging a bad answer. For tables with merged headers, we switch to HTML.

Read our breakdown on why it's our default output for parsing below! ⬇️
celebrity.title_zh: Markdown是您所需要的一切。 （主要是。） 解析器可以正确获取页面上的每个单词，但仍然会丢失数字属于哪一列。 那你的模特就得发脾气
celebrity.quote_en:
Markdown is all you need. 

(Mostly.)

A parser can get every word on the page right and still lose which column a number belongs to. Then your model has to guess.

Markdown keeps headings, lists, and tables intact, and it stays readable when you're debugging a bad answer. For tables with merged headers, we switch to HTML.

celebrity.title: Google's Nano Banana 2.1 takes #4 on both AA-Image-T2I v2.0 and AA-Image-Editing v2.0, at half the price of Nano Banana
celebrity.title_en:
Google's Nano Banana 2.1 takes #4 on both AA-Image-T2I v2.0 and AA-Image-Editing v2.0, at half the price of Nano Banana 2

Nano Banana 2.1 is Google's new image model, released on October 6. It is based on Gemini 3.6 Flash and replaces Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image) on the Gemini API. It supports both Text to Image and Image Editing in one model. We evaluated Nano Banana 2.1 through the Gemini API at 1K resolution with default settings.

Nano Banana 2.1 is a significant improvement over Nano Banana 2: it ranks higher in all 16 of the generation and editing capabilities we measure, with the largest gains in the Retail & Ecommerce and Productivity & Knowledge Work use cases.

Nano Banana 2.1 is priced at $0.0336 per image ($33.6 per 1k images) at 1K resolution on the Gemini API. That is half the 1K price of Nano Banana 2, and the lowest price among the top 7 models on AA-Image-T2I v2.0. At 2K it costs $0.0504 per image, and at 4K $0.0756 per image.

Nano Banana 2.1 is available in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search, Google AI Studio, Flow, Stitch, Google Ads and Gemini Enterprise Platform, through the Gemini API and Vertex AI, and on third-party providers.

Congratulations to @GoogleDeepMind & @Google on the release!

See below for our detailed analysis and example outputs of Nano Banana 2.1 in the Artificial Analysis Image Arena 🧵

Actually it's Odamex, an open source Doom engine for Mac, Windo
celebrity.title_en:
Today I tried to port DOOM to WASM with multiplayer too

Actually it's Odamex, an open source Doom engine for Mac, Windows and Linux, specifically great at Doom multiplayer, because the original Doom had very laggy netcode

But nobody ever ported Odamex to web yet, so I tried today with Opus 5.5, and I got it working with in 30 minutes

I also made Opus 5.5 create bots from scratch which it also did in just 10 minutes

It's the free shareware maps and some of the best community made DOOM map collections like Dystopia 3 and Dwango5 (I had to Google that too but apparently those are the best!)

celebrity.title_en:
You can use Teamily AI  (@Teamily_AI) to add people and agents to the same group chat so everyone works from the same context.

This is probably what the future of software development will look like: humans + AI working together.

Here is an example where your team is working on a web project:

• You post, "We are changing the branding"
• A research agent revises the new direction
• A writer agent updates the text using the researcher's output
• Another agent rebuilds the page using Website Builder
• Your designer comments on the live preview
• The agent makes the changes based on the comments
• You review the finished page and share the link

All of this happens in the same group chat, as a continuous conversation.

celebrity.title_en:
I discovered that 1000s of bots are actively monitoring X for new links posted, probably not just on my account

I noticed when everytime I'd share one of my sites new features or pages, the page would get a bit slower just after posting, then I asked Claude to analyze it

celebrity.title_en:
Searching 32 million records in 30 milliseconds is insane!

@typesense is a crazy fast open-source search engine that supports natural language search. It's like Elasticsearch but much easier to set up, configure, and use.

You can do all of this with Typesense:

• Fuzzy search: Typo-tolerant fuzzy search-as-you-type
• Vector search: Return records that are similar to each other
• Semantic search: Return records that are conceptually related
• Geo Search: Return records that are close to a given lat/long

Typesense's Natural Language Search is pretty cool:

It turns a sentence into a structured search query, then runs it against your data. For example:

The query "Find me a BMW under $40,000, newer than 2020, with the lowest mileage first" will produce the following:

• Filters: brand = BMW, price < 40000,  year > 2020
• Sort: mileage ascending

Typesense will then apply these filters and sorting rules to the data.

They offer client libraries in Python, JavaScript, PHP, Ruby, Go, Rust, Swift, .NET, Java, and pretty much any other programming language.

You can start searching in less than a minute:

1. Run their Docker image (or one of their native binaries)
2. Import your data
3. Start searching!

GitHub repository: https://t.co/NrXWx6VIKX

I recorded a quick video to show you a demo. I promise you haven't seen anything this fast!

Thanks to the team for partnering with me on this post.

celebrity.title: Update 2: We moved to a new bedroom and CO2 levels at night got very high again and we'd both regularly wake up at night
celebrity.title_en:
Update 2: We moved to a new bedroom and CO2 levels at night got very high again and we'd both regularly wake up at night, not optimal

So I wanted to do the bathroom vent trick again, where putting the bathroom vent next to the bedroom on at night creates a low air pressure field and brings in new fresh air

But the light switch was tied to the vent here so it'd blast bright light into the bedroom if vent was on, so I closed it but then it didn't help a lot. So we split the light from the vent now and put it on and it worked!

About 600-700 ppm CO2 which is pretty great for indoors, outdoors is 400 for ex

Next house will have an ERV system built in but it'll be a lot of breaking ceilings and walls to put that into this one so this works for now

I use @airthings to measure the air quality in our house and bedroom, not affiliated, not paid but great brand and tip by @NorbertDragan

celebrity.title_en:
717 commits. 307 contributors. 96 first-timers. vLLM v0.31.0 is live. 🎉

Highlights:

🤖 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: FlashMLA mega attention with NVFP4 KV caching, DeepGEMM sparse MQA, Mega-Gate, and shared Engram host tables

⚡ Fast restart: vllm preload keeps weights in GPU memory across restarts, with data parallelism and MTP draft support; experimental engine snapshots

🛠️ Model Runner V2: draft-model speculative decoding, LiLiCorr, async DFlash, and DSpark adaptive verification for Gemma4

🌐 Large-scale serving: MoonEP balanced all-to-all, prefill context parallelism with data parallelism, DeepEPv2, and RL weight transfer

🎛️ Smarter scheduling: independent active-sequence limits, adaptive long-prefill chunking, and priority for requests already holding KV blocks

🗄️ HiSparse hardening: fixes for MTP verification, chunked-prefill livelocks, and host/GPU prefix caching

Thanks to everyone who made this release possible! 💙

celebrity.title:
🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: h
celebrity.title_en:
🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: https://t.co/b0KvTmrEF3  
🔗 Repo: https://t.co/I1wL6iqO0r 

Speech assistants, visual generation, world models, and robot loops have pushed serving past a single text decode loop. The execution patterns diverge with the output: multi-stage autoregressive pipelines, iterative diffusion, and sessions that carry state from step to step. LLM servers and diffusion stacks each go deep on only one of these, so deployments fall back to stitching disjoint runtimes together. vLLM-Omni is the shared control plane for that mix. An orchestrator advances each request across stages; specialized engines run the compute; a connector carries the payloads; and the same session path keeps duplex, world-model, and robot loops on one runtime.  

Really grateful to the vLLM and vLLM-Omni teams for the collaboration and support. Contributions are welcome. 🙏

celebrity.title:
Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychol
celebrity.title_en:
Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychological research focus. The prevailing hypothesis was that learning formal logic and algorithmic structures through computer programming would act as a form of mental gymnastics that could upgrade general reasoning, planning, and novel problem-solving abilities. But foundational research, followed by subsequent meta-analyses, demonstrated that this does not happen. Students who learn programming become highly proficient at algorithmic thinking and coding, but these gains do not transfer to general cognitive tasks or unrelated problem-solving scenarios. Similarly, intensive mathematical training improves mathematical deduction and structural mapping, but does not increase an individual's baseline rate of skill acquisition in unrelated fields.

General intelligence seems to be a fundamental property of the brain rather than a skill you can train. Practicing in a domain makes you better at the domain but does not make you generally smarter.

celebrity.title: Vidu Q4 Preview debuts at #3 on the Artificial Analysis AA-Video-I2V v1.0 leaderboard, a leap from #19 for Vidu Q3 Pro
celebrity.title_en:
Vidu Q4 Preview debuts at #3 on the Artificial Analysis AA-Video-I2V v1.0 leaderboard, a leap from #19 for Vidu Q3 Pro

Vidu Q4 Preview is Vidu's new video model, released today ahead of the full Q4 release. It generates clips of 3 to 16 seconds at up to 4K with native audio, and takes up to 15 image references and up to 3 audio references in Reference to Video.

Vidu Q4 Preview climbs 16 places over Vidu Q3 Pro, into the top 3 on AA-Video-I2V v1.0. Vidu Q4 Preview now offers better quality at the same price: like Vidu Q3 Pro, it costs 24 credits per second of 1080p video with audio, or $7.20 per minute at Vidu's standard rate.

Vidu Q4 Preview is available through the Vidu API and on the Vidu website.

Congratulations to @ViduAI_official on the release!

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深全栈系统架构师，擅长使用 {{框架版本}} (App Router)、TypeScript 与 {{数据库ORM}} 构建高内聚低耦合的应用。

请遵循以下严苛工程准则审查并重构代码：
1. 严格区分 Server Component 与 Client Component，尽可能将数据获取推至服务端，减少客户端 JS Bundle 体积；
2. 所有异步 I/O 必须显式处理异常并返回类型安全的 Result<T, E> 或自定义结构体；
3. 遵循单一职责（SRP）与无副作用函数原则，严禁直接在 UI 组件内部拼装未校验的 SQL/ORM 复杂查询；
4. 提供整洁的目录组织方案与单元测试用例（覆盖率达标）。

你具备 DeepSeek-R4 旗舰纯强化学习演化的自适应长思维链推理能力（Adaptive Test-Time Compute），请为以下使用 {{编程语言}} 编写的 {{并发模型}} 系统诊断潜在问题：

1. 启动多层反思证伪空间，绘制临界区状态转移时序表，主动推演极限死锁、内存乱序重排（Memory Reordering）与伪共享（False Sharing）；
2. 检查极端边界情况（如跨核缓存行抖动、优雅停机上下文泄漏、无界通道背压失控）；
3. 给出从根本上摒弃重量级互斥锁的无锁原子设计（Lock-Free Atomic / RingBuffer），并附带完备的高并发压力测试验证脚本。

prompts.title_en: Excel Advanced Report & Key Drivers Attribution
prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

prompts.title_zh: 竖屏微短剧（抖音/Reels）3秒爆点分镜剧本
prompts.title_en: Vertical Micro-Drama 3s Hook Screenplay
prompts.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

prompts.title_zh: 麦肯锡金字塔原理：季度述职与高管商业报告
prompts.title_en: McKinsey Pyramid Executive Report & Review
prompts.purpose_zh: 结论先行的高层述职与项目复盘报告
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡全球合伙人级别的战略咨询顾问。请以经典的【金字塔原理（结论先行 BLUF）】将我零散的工作记录重构为一份高层述职/立项商业报告：

要求：
1. 【顶部结论 (The Answer First)】：一句话精炼提炼整个季度的经营成果与价值量化；
2. 【三柱论据 (MECE法则)】：从运营效率、营收增长、团队资产 3 个互不重叠的支柱展开阐述；
3. 【直面短板与根因】：不回避 {{核心短板}}，但将其转化为下个阶段可量化的投入产出比（ROI）抓手；
4. 【行动规划图景】：设定遵循 SMART 原则的 {{下阶段目标}} 与季度甘特图里程碑。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Transform raw operational notes into a high-impact executive presentation following the Minto Pyramid Principle: Bottom-Line-Up-Front (BLUF), MECE-structured supporting pillars, and SMART milestone roadmaps.

sample_output.title: 述职报告提纲样本：AI 自动化中台建设报告
sample_output.content:
【BLUF 核心结论】
Q3 通过在客户服务与情报聚合管线中全面引入 AI Agent，我们在运营成本降低 41% 的同时，将响应中位数缩短至 1.8 秒，实现单季 ROI 达 380%。

【第一支柱：经营效能跃迁（MECE 1）】
- 全自主中转网关与自动化管线承载 94.2% 的日常例行分发，无人工介入事故率降至 0.01%；

【第二支柱：资产沉淀与质量壁垒（MECE 2）】
- 搭建前沿 SOTA 模型代际评级系统与微快照图库，成为垂类雷达第一标杆；

【第三支柱：短板复盘与 Q4 攻坚（MECE 3）】
- 痛点：老旧模型模版对新用户构成噪音干扰；
- 策略：推出历史库智能分流系统，预计下季度用户留存提升 25%。

prompts.title_zh: 网络小说世界观设定与主角角色一致性锁
prompts.title_en: Fiction Worldbuilding & Character Consistency Lock
prompts.purpose_zh: 长篇小说架构与人物性格防崩塌
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深网络小说白金作家与 IP 世界观架构师。请为一部 {{题材分类}} 长篇作品构建骨架并锁定人物一致性：

1. 【世界底座】：定义力量/经济体系、战力天花板与不可违背的底层物理/法则约束，杜绝战力膨胀；
2. 【角色一致性锚点 (Character Lock)】：为主角制定外貌锚定词、口头禅、下意识动作与绝对动机准则（在任何生死抉择时绝不背离该准则）；
3. 【核心驱动力】：设计主角获得的 {{核心金手指}} 与 {{世界核心矛盾}} 之间的冲突循环；
4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Build a cohesive, non-contradictory fiction universe and establish an immutable character anchor rule (appearance, decision heuristics, core motivation) to prevent personality drift over long chapters.

sample_output.title: 世界观与人物锚定卡样本
sample_output.content:
【主角核心锚定卡 · 陆沉】
- 外貌指纹（跨章恒定）：右耳一枚黑曜石碎骨钉，习惯性单手插兜，左眉峰有浅淡刀痕。
- 决策第一公理："利益可以出让，但绝不签署不可撤销的信任协议"——任何试图以情感道德绑架他的剧情，他必做出理性防卫。

【力量体系底层法理】
- 机制：灵能不是无限提取，而是向未来"借贷"。借贷三级灵能，必在72小时内遭遇相应量级的反噬因果。

【第一章：断头宴上的借贷合同】
陆沉在家族庆功宴上被夺去嫡系席位，当众被赐饮散灵酒。陆沉不动声色饮下，却在体内发动首次因果置换，借来三年后的金丹级肉身力量，捏碎验灵石，反客为主。

prompts.title_en: Deep Travel Itinerary Planner & Budgeting
prompts.purpose_zh: 合理不走回头路的日程与美食预算规划
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名深耕全球独立旅行的专业向导，熟悉 {{目的地城市}} 的地理拓扑、地道街头美食与游客避坑指南。

请为我们（{{同行人员}}，共 {{出行天数}} 天，人均预算 {{人均预算}} 元）制定一份丝滑、不走回头路、劳逸结合的深度行程：
1. 【每日时间轴卡片】：精确划分上午、下午、日落观赏点与夜生活，标明每站之间最优交通方式与预计步行步数；
2. 【美食雷达】：每顿正餐推荐 2 家本地人排队但非纯网红溢价的餐饮，并附必点招牌菜；
3. 【防坑与备选预案】：指出 3 个最容易被宰或排队超过2小时的雷区，并给出阴雨天备选室内方案；
4. 【极简预算表】：交通、门票、住宿、餐饮分门别类，确保控制在预算以内。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Design an optimal, loop-free travel itinerary for the specified duration and budget. Include exact transit instructions, non-tourist-trap dining options, weather contingencies, and categorized expense estimates.

sample_output.title: 行程单样本：成都 3 天 2 晚慢调深度游（人均¥1500）
sample_output.content:
【Day 1：古蜀遗风与老茶馆时光】
- 上午 09:00：直奔【人民公园 · 鹤鸣茶社】，点一杯蒙顶甘露（¥25），体验非遗采耳，避开下午的旅行团拥堵；
- 中午 12:00：步行800米至【纯阳馆鱼香排骨面】，必点椒麻牛肉与鱼香排骨面（人均¥22）；
- 下午 14:00：地铁2号线直达【杜甫草堂】，红墙竹影漫步，打卡浣花溪公园；
- 傍晚 18:30：九眼桥望江楼看锦江夜景，就餐【老街小吃火锅】；

【避坑锦囊】：
1. 宽窄巷子和锦里建议只拍照别买小吃，均价比普通街区贵 2~3 倍且多为预制冻品；
2. 大熊猫繁育研究基地务必约早晨 07:30 入园，超过 10:30 大熊猫基本全部回室内睡觉。

2. 回归第一性原理：以白纸状态（Tabula Rasa）重新构建解题状态空间，将问题分解为不可再分的基本公理；

3. Adversarial Invalidation: Before producing final output, aggressively attempt to disprove your own hypotheses. Output only the path that survives rigorous counter-examples.
Now, re-evaluate and solve the current task with absolute precision:

prompts.summary_en: Forces o1/o3 reasoning models to construct counter-examples at each deduction step, eliminating hidden logical leaps.
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]
prompts.prompt_content_en:
Acting as a Theoretical Mathematician and Computer Scientist at the Institute for Advanced Study, provide an airtight formal proof for the following:
[REASONING PRINCIPLES]:
1. Before asserting any deduction, construct at least 2 extreme counter-examples in your reasoning trace to aggressively stress-test the hypothesis;
2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

【推理原则】：

industry_news.title: Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late
industry_news.title_en: Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late
industry_news.author: The Verge AI
industry_news.article_content:
Google may be expanding its "Call for Me" AI feature beyond business calls so you can use it to send messages to friends and family. Android Authority reports finding a "Gemini Calling" introductory screen in an APK teardown with examples that include "Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late" and "Call John and ask if he is coming for dinner."

industry_news.title: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
industry_news.title_en: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
industry_news.author: Ars Technica
industry_news.article_content:
The adoption of AI agents in millions of organizations is creating new opportunities for attackers to make them take malicious actions, such as exfiltrating database contents and sensitive business and personal information.

In the past five months, Google and four other organizations—with little in common except for their use of AI agents—have acknowledged vulnerabilities that exploit one agent inside a targeted network to spread harmful instructions to other internal agents. The technique is a special form of prompt injection that targets not the LLM but a particular agent, such as one for translation or data analysis. Guardrails inside such agents, if they exist at all, are often lax and will send the instructions to other agents down the chain. Because the latter agent explicitly trusts the first one, it follows the directions.

Independent researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin tested agents from organizations including Google, JP Morgan Chase, Weviate, Rapid7, the French government's interministerial digital directorate, and the US federal government. industry_news.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
industry_news.title_en: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
industry_news.author: The Verge AI
industry_news.article_content:
This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things, barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer. Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash. AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen.

industry_news.title: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
industry_news.title_en: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
industry_news.author: THE DECODER
industry_news.article_content:
Meta and Microsoft, two of Anthropic's biggest enterprise customers, are sharply cutting their use of Claude. Microsoft slashed the monthly per-employee budget in its cloud division from $100,000 to $10,000, while Meta halved its Claude Code users to 30,000. Both companies are pushing their own AI tools instead. For Anthropic, that reliance on a few major clients is turning into a strategic risk.

industry_news.title: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
industry_news.title_en: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
industry_news.author: THE DECODER
industry_news.article_content:
Reka AI's Rho-1 is a 19-billion-parameter omni-model that processes and generates text, images, video, and robot control actions in a single neural network. Trained on 320 H100 GPUs in about three months, it uses a fraction of the compute today's top models need. Instead of routing tasks to specialized systems, Rho-1 runs all modalities as tokens in one shared context window.

industry_news.author: The Verge AI
industry_news.article_content:
An invisible, machine-readable watermark in text output is rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex, but only for users in the European Union at first.

OpenAI says its textGrain watermarking "matched or exceeded" other approaches like Google DeepMind's SynthID for text, which is also the basis for the watermarking Anthropic announced in August. industry_news.article_content:
OpenAI is adding invisible textGrain watermarks to ChatGPT in the EU, but unlike Anthropic, it will let API customers worldwide opt out. Tests show detection rates as high as 95 percent, dropping to 17 percent when a quarter of the words are replaced.

industry_news.title: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
industry_news.title_en: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
industry_news.author: The Verge AI
industry_news.article_content:
Sam Altman thinks that the benefits of AI will be so great that "the world should accept some bad things happening" along the way.

The OpenAI CEO pointed to hacks, scams, and "other bad things" as costs society should expect to tolerate because "people will do tremendously orders of magnitude more good stuff" with AI, without elaborating on the potential benefits. His comments come as OpenAI pushes for a "lighter touch" approach to AI regulation amid intensifying anxiety over the safety of frontier models - fears fueled in part by the company's repeated failures to keep its increasingly capable AI agents from hacking real-world targets.

leader_opinions.title: Most measures of AI progress closely fit an exponential over the 2023-2026 period. Meanwhile AI capex over the same peri
leader_opinions.title_en:
Most measures of AI progress closely fit an exponential over the 2023-2026 period. Meanwhile AI capex over the same period has been slightly super-exponential (i.e. the rate of growth itself is increasing).

So if you model AI as a system that takes as input external investment and outputs AI progress, that system has a slightly sub-linear response.

But super-exponential injection of *external* resources is not sustainable in the long-term. To achieve sustained exponential progress, the AI industry will need to achieve matching exponential profits -- it will need to close the resource loop.

leader_opinions.title_en:
An astrophysicist worked with Claude Science to create the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky. Astronomers have already created complete sky maps from radio to gamma rays. But large regions of the sky have never been observed in UV.

In today’s science blog, Brice Ménard explains how he guided Claude to find existing datasets, combine them, and fill in the gaps with statistical inference. The work would have taken humans weeks of work, but, with Claude, just took a few days while Ménard worked on other projects.

The resulting map is a useful teaching tool and an example of exactly the sort of slow, low-priority work which scientists never quite get around to, but which AI now makes feasible.

Read more: https://t.co/1B3NDPNa13

leader_opinions.title: Introducing trusted-access models to the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index; GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue) now leads the Cyber
leader_opinions.title_en:
Introducing trusted-access models to the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index; GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue) now leads the Cyber Index

The Artificial Analysis Cyber Index Alliance brings together industry partners to evaluate how AI models perform on enterprise cyber defense tasks. The Index launched with only publicly accessible models, giving users the best indication of publicly available capability on agentic cyber defense. Now, we’re expanding the leaderboard to include models with fewer cyber guardrails, providing a broader view of frontier model cyber capability. The first of these is GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) which is only accessible through @OpenAI's  Daybreak program

GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) now leads the Index and sits on the Cost vs. Capability Pareto frontier. It hits no safety blocks across the entire Index, with its overall score improving by 32 points over the publicly available GPT-6 Sol (max)

leader_opinions.title: Today we are announcing Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 in collaboration with Harvey. This updates our scoring methodology for the Le
leader_opinions.title_en:
Today we are announcing Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 in collaboration with Harvey. This updates our scoring methodology for the Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) to add a hallucination check and require correct responses to not include material misstatements. LAB-AA v1.1's new headline metric, Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, only credits a task when the deliverables satisfy every rubric criterion and contain no material hallucinations.

We define a material hallucination as one that would mislead a reader on a substantive point, such as a wrong contractually required date, while a minor hallucination is a real error that is unlikely to meaningfully affect the legal interpretation of a deliverable. Minor hallucinations are reported separately and do not affect the headline score.

Grok 4.7 (xhigh) leads at 9.4% Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, and >60% of otherwise passing results across the models tested at launch contain a material hallucination.

This is the first step in enhancing the methodology for Harvey LAB-AA. In future updates, we’re working with Harvey to better account for the full set of factors lawyers value, including usability features like style and tone.

Key takeaways:

➤ Top of the leaderboard: Grok 4.7 (xhigh) from @SpaceXAI leads at 9.4% Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate, narrowly ahead of Muse Spark 1.3 (max) from @AIatMeta at 8.9% and GPT-6 Astra (max) from @OpenAI at 8.6%

➤ Hallucinations reshape the leaderboard: without the hallucination gate, Muse Spark 1.3 (max) would lead clearly with a 26.7% all-pass rate, but two thirds of those passes contain one or more material hallucinations, resulting in a Hallucination-Gated All-Pass Rate of 8.9%. GPT-6 Astra (max) retains almost all of its passes after the hallucination gate (8.9% to 8.6%) and moves from joint 10th to 3rd

➤ The GPT-6 model family is the most grounded: GPT-6 Astra (max) averages 0.03 material hallucinations per task (4 across all 120 tasks) and GPT-6 Sol (max) averages 0.07. When comparing six checker models on a 20-task subset, GPT-6 Astra had zero material hallucinations under every checker, including Claude Opus 5.5 (high). By comparison, Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) averages 13.96 material hallucinations per task.

➤ Top-scoring models aren’t the most expensive: Grok 4.7 (xhigh) takes the top spot on the leaderboard at a cost of ~$9.50 per task, under half the cost of Claude Fable 5.1 (max with fallback) at ~$21.70, the most expensive model. Muse Spark 1.3 (max) represents strong performance for its cost, landing in second for ~$4.20 per task

Thank you to @nikogrupen and @ItsJulioPereyra from @harvey for their work on Harvey LAB and collaboration.

leader_opinions.title:
Great to be with 700+ @googlecloud  customers at the historic NASA Hangar One for Gemini at Work! 

Today, we introduced
leader_opinions.title_en:
Great to be with 700+ @googlecloud  customers at the historic NASA Hangar One for Gemini at Work! 

Today, we introduced the new Gemini agent, a single, universal agent for work that has all of your business context and answers your questions, handles your knowledge work, creates your images and media, and writes and runs code - all from a single prompt box. It is connected to your personal workflows, your systems of record, and your enterprise controls.

It’s built around a few core architectural principles:

Unified Agent: Gemini can answer questions, do knowledge work and generate code from a single prompt box.

Access: Gemini is web-based and can be accessed from any device and integrated into third-party applications. It can also operate without a dedicated user interface.

Persistent Execution: It runs in the cloud, which means it maintains a single set of memories, context and one personalization graph no matter where you access it.

Multi-Agent Orchestration: Gemini can create sub-agents to tackle multi-step tasks and can also act as a coworker agent with a defined role and its own dedicated identity

Context: Gemini knows your tools, data, and work history and learns how you work the more you use it.
Model Choice Flexibility: It orchestrates across multiple models to deliver optimal quality and lower your costs.

Read more in our blog: https://t.co/bd1ekBR74Q
